question.text: This British Major General surrendered following the Siege of Yorktown.
question.clue: This man's most famous act was actually performed by a proxy, General Charles O'Hara, who surrendered to Benjamin Lincoln, the subordinate of George Washington.

swap.leadin: The command "Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes" was issued during this battle.
swap.text: Name this June 1775 battle in which American forces lost to a British army on the outskirts of Boston. The location of this battle was actually at Breed's Hill, not at its namesake location.
swap.clue: William Prescott constructed a defensive redoubt at this battle, which resulted in the dismissal of Thomas Gage.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women in early American history.
question.text: This possibly-legendary woman took her husband's place loading cannons at the Battle of Monmouth during the American Revolution. Her nickname comes from her previous role as a water carrier.
question.answerHtml: Molly Pitcher [or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley; or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley]
question.clue: The Battle of Monmouth also saw this American woman aid the Continental Army fight the British. This woman, whose identity was thought to be Mary Ludwig Hays, has an iconic image of her loading a canon.

swap.leadin: It included skirmishes at Freeman's Farm and Bemis Heights, and is commonly considered the turning point in the war.
swap.text: Name this campaign to take New York, with American Revolutionary forces led by Horatio Gates.
swap.clue: John Burgoyne surrendered to Horatio Gates after this campaign.

question.leadin: Answer the following about John Adams's predecessor, George Washington.
question.text: George Washington was a victor at this Revolutionary War battle on Christmas Day, in which his troops were able to take the namesake town after crossing the Delaware.
question.clue: There is no historical evidence that one side got drunk the night before this battle, although more than one thousand Hessians were surprised and captured by the Revolutionary Army at this battle.

swap.text: The first major American casualty was this Major General of Irish descent, who led the attack of Quebec City with Benedict Arnold.
swap.clue: At the second Battle of Quebec, during the Revolutionary War, Benedict Arnold commanded the American troops along with this Irish-born general, who was killed in action.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Espionage Front during the American Revolution.
question.text: This American spy who was hanged in New York after stating "I only regret, that I have but one life to lose for my country"
question.clue: Robert Rogers recognized this man in a tavern, where he was apprehended by the Queen's Rangers and hung shortly afterwards.

swap.leadin: This man was the only Founding Father to sign the First Continental Congress's Continental Association, the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, and the Constitution.
swap.text: Name this Connecticut representative at the Constitutional Convention, more famous for brokering the Great Compromise between the Virginia and New Jersey Plans, which created the bicameral legislature.
swap.clue: This man's son-in-law, Simeon Baldwin, succeeded him in a post of which he was the inaugural holder; that post was Mayor of New Haven, Connecticut.

question.leadin: Name these northern battles of the American Revolution.
question.text: At this creek on the Pennsylvania-Delaware border, the British won a September 1777 battle for access to Philadelphia.
question.clue: General von Knyphausen led the flanking attack that ended this battle, which was followed by a defeat for Anthony Wayne known as the Paoli Massacre.

swap.text: This loser at Saratoga was known as "Gentleman Johnny" and took Fort Ticonderoga and Fort Edward before losing at Saratoga.
swap.clue: This British general commanded at Saratoga. He was to rejoin William Howe in Albany following the battle, but was abandoned by Howe and had to surrender outright.

question.text: In 1814 Thomas Macdonough defeated a British Fleet under Captain Downie in this battle foiling George Prevost's planned invasion of New York.
question.clue: Before this battle, which was part of the siege of , William Prescott fortified the wrong location leading to a confusion over its name.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the Revolutionary War in New Jersey.
swap.text: This American general commanded an outnumbered forward guard at Monmouth and later took Stony Point. After the Revolution, he defeated Little Turtle and Blue Jacket at the Battle of Fallen Timbers.
swap.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

question.leadin: "Remember the ladies" by answering the following about women from early American history.
question.text: A woman from this family, Mercy Warren, advocated for a Bill of Rights in her Observations on the New Constitution. Her brother from this family, James, coined the phrase "taxation without representation is tyranny."
question.clue: A woman from this family married James Warren and was the first woman to write a history of the American Revolution.

swap.text: After Leclerc died of yellow fever, he was replaced by a cruel military commander from this family. A French count from this family led the U.S. naval blockade at the Battle of Yorktown.
swap.clue: This general's son surrendered to Jacques Dessalines shortly before the declaration of Haitian independence.

question.leadin: Name some people who participated in the southern theatre of the American Revolutionary War.
question.text: This commander's surprise attack on a British camp at the Battle of Black Mingo was given away by the sound of his horses crossing a wooden bridge, but he still eluded capture by Banastre Tarleton for the duration of the war.
question.clue: This man commanded the right flank of Nathaniel Green's army at the Battle of Eutaw Springs after leading many raids against British troops stationed between the Pee Dee and Stanee Rivers, preventing full British control of South Carolina.

swap.leadin: During this event, one party made a speech stating that no one should try to "open the floodgates of civil discord and deluge our rising empire in blood."
swap.text: Identify this event in which the Continental Army threatened the newly formed United States government due to uncertainty over them receiving their pensions. George Washington managed to quell it with a good short speech.
swap.clue: It followed the rejection of an impost amendment supported by its possible real organizers, Robert Morris and Alexander Hamilton.

question.text: A Founding Father with this surname helped write the Commissioner's Plan and served as chair of the Erie Canal Commission after writing the preamble to the constitution. A financier with this surname went broke in a D.C. land scheme that caused the Panic of 1796.
question.clue: Another man with this surname represented Pennsylvania at the 1787 Constitutional Convention.

swap.leadin: Identify these treaties with Native Americans FTPE.
swap.text: The first such treaty, it was signed on the site of a battle of St. Leger's campaign that ended at Oriskany. It dissolved the Iroquois Confederacy and forced the Six Nations to turn their land over to the State of New York in 1784.
swap.clue: This 1768 treaty between the British, represented by William Johnson, and the Iroquois moved the boundary line west of the Appalachians. It was not terribly effective, either, though, as it led to Dunmore's War.

question.text: Lee also led troops at this last major battle in the Carolinas during the Revolution. Despite winning a tactical victory here over Nathanael Greene, Alexander Stewart was forced to retreat to Charleston until the end of the war.
question.clue: Often called the bloodiest battle of the Revolution, this September 1781 assault on Alexander Stewart deteriorated into a raid on the British wine supplies, but nonetheless trapped Stewart's forces in Charlestown for the rest of the war.

swap.text: This author of Extracts from the Virginia Charters wrote Virginia's Declaration of Rights, and explained his refusal to sign at the Convention in his "Objections to this Constitution of Government."
swap.clue: The concepts in this politician's Fairfax Resolves influenced a document he demanded that introduced the right to bear arms.
